newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar likely to be directionless in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely to be directionless in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be directionless against the yen in Asia on Monday after wild gyrations on Friday following U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks, dealers said.

The late recovery in U.S. stocks on Friday after earlier dive relieved traders and should support the dollar's downside here, but lingering worries that booming U.S. financial markets could burst may cap dollar's top at 113.50 yen, they said.
"It would be very difficult to take either long or short positions here with a clear view after the large fluctuations on Friday," said a trust bank dealer.

"Even though the dollar's bottom was confirmed after its recovery in New York, there is hesitation to test the upside strongly because of the instability in U.S. financial markets," said the trust bank dealer.
The dollar fell to low as 111.73 yen and 1.5280 marks in Europe on Friday after Greenspan warned about "irrational exuberance" infecting financial markets.
The comments were taken as a hint that the central bank might boost interest rates to cool things down, but a surprisingly weak U.S. payrolls report calmed worries about an interest rate hike.
Amid a lack of fresh factors and economic data scheduled for today, dealers here will closely watch developments in the Japanese stock and bond markets, dealers said.

The dollar's strength against European currencies is likely to give indirect support to the dollar/yen rate. Japanese investor dollar buying interest could stay intact at the 112 yen level, dealers said.

"The trend of a firming dollar against European currencies hasn't changed, which could support the dollar/yen rate," said a city bank dealer. The dollar is likely to have a support at 1.5450 marks but be capped at 1.5550 marks in Asia.
